title: Sales Enablement: Prospect & Enterprise Playbook - Positioning, Competitive Briefs, Pitch Decks, Pricing Guidance, Case Studies, Security FAQ
author: Evelyn Brooks
content:
Summary:
This playbook centralizes the sales enablement assets and messaging for prospect and enterprise conversations. It combines positioning, competitive brief guidance, a recommended pitch-deck storyboard, pricing guidance, two turnkey case studies, and a prospect-focused security FAQ. Use this doc when prepping discovery calls, demos, and procurement conversations.

Audience:
- AE/SE teams working on SMB through enterprise deals
- Solutions and Partner Engineers supporting POCs
- Marketing and product for alignment on claims and proof points

Owner & Escalations:
- Primary owner: go-to-market / Sales Enablement (Evelyn Brooks)
- Technical reviewer / escalation: Product Solutions (Jared Kim)
- Security contact: Security & Compliance (Lena Ortiz)

1) Positioning & Core Messaging
Purpose: Provide a tight, repeatable set of value statements and evidence tailored to engineering-driven buyers and procurement stakeholders.

Elevator (30s):
Redwood Inference is a developer-first inference platform that makes LLM-powered features predictable and economical in production. We provide a unified runtime and operations layer across hosted API, reserved Dedicated capacity, and Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments so teams can standardize on one API surface while optimizing latency, cost, and compliance.

Value pillars (customer-facing):
- Production-first performance: predictable latency SLOs (p50/p95 targets), consistent throughput, and rapid failover paths.
- Cost control & unit economics: batching, KV prefix caching, and quantization recommendations reduce per-token cost without sacrificing quality.
- Unified deployment flexibility: move from hosted to Dedicated or Private with minimal code changes and consistent observability.
- Enterprise-ready security & governance: KMS integration, audit logs, RBAC, and region/data residency controls.

Key messages by persona:
- Engineering/ML Engineers: "Same API across environments + high-throughput runtime = less operational work and predictable performance at scale."
- Platform/Infra: "Dedicated pools, autoscaling policies, and easy migration allow you to consolidate inference workloads with capacity predictability."
- Procurement/Security: "Private deployments and compliance packages (SOC2, contractual controls, audit evidence) support regulated workloads."

2) Competitive Briefs (three quick battlecards)
Guidance: use the bullets below as the core of one-page battlecards for SDR/AE/SEs. Include proof points (benchmarks, customer wins) when available.

Competitor: Public Cloud Managed Endpoints
- Competitor strength: wide availability, deep cloud ecosystem, integrated model access.
- Redwood win themes: predictable unit economics via batching/quantization, unified offering across hosted/dedicated/private, transparent per-route performance dashboards and rollout controls.
- Key objection response: "If you're optimizing for predictable latency and cost at scale, Redwood's Dedicated pools and runtime kernels reduce tail latency and token-cost more effectively than generic managed endpoints. We can show side-by-side p95 and cost-per-token comparisons on your workload."

Competitor: Inference Runtime Vendors / Open Source Ops
- Competitor strength: control, lower software license cost initially.
- Redwood win themes: opinionated production runtime + orchestration, built-in model catalog and verified profiles, integrated observability and cost analytics, enterprise support and rollouts.
- Key objection response: "Open-source runtimes require significant integration and ongoing tuning to match production SLOs. Redwood provides the runtime plus the orchestration, monitoring, and support needed to run reliably in prod."

Competitor: LLM API-focused Providers (simplicity-first)
- Competitor strength: extremely low friction for prototypes and small usage.
- Redwood win themes: performance guarantees, deployment flexibility, and advanced operational controls for scale and regulated data.
- Key objection response: "For prototypes, simplicity helps - but when customers hit scale, they need predictable throughput, cost, and private deployments. Redwood bridges the gap from prototyping to production."

3) Pitch Deck Guidance (recommended 8-slide storyboard)
Use this sequence for technical buyers + executive sponsors. Keep slides concise with a single clear chart or metric per slide.

Recommended slides:
1. Title & TL;DR (1 sentence value prop + 2 outcomes: latency, cost, compliance)
2. Customer problem / patterns we see (burstiness, cold-starts, cost growth, audit/compliance needs)
3. Redwood platform overview (hosted API, Dedicated pools, Private deployment) - one architecture diagram
4. Performance & cost proof (sample p50/p95, tokens/sec, cost-per-token improvements vs baseline) - include a small benchmark table
5. Migration & rollout story (pin versions, canary, automatic fallback to cheaper variant) - short steps for a POC -> prod path
6. Security & compliance checklist (KMS, SOC2, VPC, audit logs, region controls)
7. Pricing model and example TCO (see pricing guidance section)
8. Case study / customer outcome + ask (POC request: N users, X tokens/day, 6-week success criteria)

Pitching tips for SEs:
- Always ask: "What are your target p50/p95 latency SLOs and expected tokens/day?" Use answers to tailor the Dedicated sizing and cost examples.
- Bring a dataset-driven benchmark when possible (we provide the eval harness template under eng/applied-ml-and-evals).
- For security-conscious buyers, lead with Private deployment options early in the conversation.

4) Pricing Guidance (high-level, example TCO and negotiation levers)
Principles:
- Be transparent about unit economics: show token pricing, embedding units, and how batching/quantization affects cost-per-inference.
- Use committed capacity (Dedicated) to trade lower unit price for predictable monthly commit.
- For Private, price as license + deployment/support; include optional managed services.

Standard SKUs (examples):
- Hosted API - pay-as-you-go: per-1k input tokens / per-1k output tokens; embeddings priced per 1k vectors.
- Dedicated - reserved monthly GPU pool: base monthly commit + overage at discounted per-token rate. Includes SLA.
- Private - platform license (annual) + deployment & support fee; optional on-prem packaging.

Example TCO table (text table for sales use):
| Scenario | Hosted cost/month | Dedicated commit/month | Private annual cost (license + ops) | Notes |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Small POC (100k tokens/day) | $3,000 | N/A | N/A | Use hosted API; POC promo credits apply |
| Scale app (5M tokens/day) | $120k | $60k/mo commit | $240k/year license + ops | Dedicated typically reduces unit cost by 30-55% depending on batching |
| Regulated (FinServ, Healthcare) | $200k | $90k/mo commit | $400k/year license + on-prem ops | Private required when strict data residency/air-gap needed |

Negotiation levers to offer:
- Commit term length (monthly vs annual) - longer terms get deeper discounts.
- Minimum throughput tiers (guaranteed GPU allocations) - affect autoscaling policy and price.
- Observability & retention add-ons - can be upsold as part of enterprise package.

5) Case Studies (select, two short vignettes)
Case study: Acme Retail - cost optimization & latency consistency
- Problem: Acme's recommendation engine moved from prototype to scale; token costs and tail latency grew unpredictably.
- Solution: Migrated to Redwood Dedicated, enabled KV prefix caching and workload-aware batching, applied a quantization profile for models where quality impact was negligible.
- Outcome: 40% reduction in per-inference cost, p95 latency improved from 820ms to 220ms, smooth autoscaling during peak events.
- Contact: Solutions Engineer who led the POC (internal): Priya Nair

Case study: FinTechCo - compliance + private deployment
- Problem: FinTechCo required data residency, audit logs for regulatory review, and on-prem inference for sensitive models.
- Solution: Deployed Redwood Private (VPC control plane + on-prem runtime), integrated customer KMS, enabled full audit logging and RBAC, and completed our standard SOC2 evidence pack.
- Outcome: Successful regulator review; inference features launched in Q4 with a 2-week deployment window; operational handover to FinTechCo platform team completed.
- Contact: Customer Success Manager (internal): Marcus Li

6) Security FAQ for Prospects (concise Q&A for buyer-facing conversations)
Q: Where does customer data live when using the hosted API?
A: Customer request data and model input/output are processed in the region selected at provisioning. We store only metadata and minimal telemetry by default; customers can opt into reduced telemetry modes or choose Dedicated/Private to ensure full data isolation.

Q: Do you provide a Private / VPC deployment?
A: Yes. Redwood offers a Private deployment option that includes a customer-managed VPC control plane and on-prem runtime packaging for air-gapped environments. See eng-private-deployments/reference-architectures for details.

Q: How is encryption handled?
A: All data in transit is TLS 1.2+/modern cipher suite. Data at rest is encrypted: hosted uses provider-managed keys, Dedicated supports customer-managed KMS, and Private supports on-prem HSM integration.

Q: What compliance standards do you meet?
A: Redwood maintains SOC2 Type II compliance and can provide evidence for enterprise diligence. Additional compliance features (data residency, contractual controls) are available as add-ons.

Q: How do you handle audit logging and access controls?
A: Audit logs capture model version, request metadata, and responses (configurable). RBAC is supported at route and team levels with SSO integration (SAML/OIDC). Logs can be forwarded to customer SIEM via secure streaming.

Q: What penetration testing and vulnerability monitoring do you perform?
A: We run quarterly third-party penetration tests and continuous vulnerability scanning on production artifacts. Test summaries and remediation timelines are available under request through Security.

Q: Can Redwood sign a data processing addendum (DPA) and standard contractual clauses?
A: Yes. Legal can scope and execute a DPA and SCCs as part of enterprise contracting. Route to finance-and-legal for contract templates.

Security contacts & escalation:
- Primary security contact for sales: Lena Ortiz (Security & Compliance)
- For immediate technical security Qs during deals: Solutions Engineering escalation (Jared Kim)

7) Sales Play & Objection Handling (cheat sheet)
- "Your costs will blow up" -> Ask for current tokens/day and model sizes; show Dedicated commit example and how batching/quantization can reduce cost.
- "We can self-host cheaper" -> Emphasize time-to-production and operational cost of maintaining performance SLAs and rollouts; offer a scoped POC to demonstrate cost and reliability delta.
- "We need regulatory evidence" -> Offer Private deployment options, provide SOC2 evidence pack, and propose a joint checklist for the procurement team.

Checklist before demo/POC kickoff:
1. Collect target p50/p95, tokens/day, models in use, and data residency requirements.
2. Decide desired deployment (hosted / dedicated / private).
3. Prepare a scoped success criteria and timeline (recommended: 6 weeks).
4. Confirm security contacts and contract lead.
